edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.mechanism: CGM improves time-in-range by exposing post-prandial spikes and nocturnal lows that fingerstick testing often misses.
edges.summary: The anchor for this edge is the 2026 Okada rct in Res Social Adm Pharm, which suggests that continuous glucose monitoring in type 2 diabetes tracks with lower risk or better outcomes for time in range. Later papers point in much the same direction, so the live uncertainty is usually about effect size or which subgroups carry the signal most strongly.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.
